Having reviewed the appointment record, our system shows that you arrived ten minutes late for your appointment. While we do ask all patients to arrive on time for their appointments to help the clinic run smoothly, we understand that delays can occasionally happen and appreciate that this is not always within a patient’s control.

Our late running policy states that the GP may not be able to see you if you are more than ten minutes late, to make sure that we can still have enough time for other patients, although we would always try to still see you if possible. We are sorry that this was not possible on this occasion.

While my experiences with the doctors have generally been positive, I cannot say the same for the reception staff.

This morning I rang regarding my prescription, as I had submitted the request a few days ago but had unfortunately run out of my medication. I asked whether anything could be done to speed up the process so that I could receive my prescription today. The receptionist I spoke to, Emina, repeatedly told me that nothing could be done, that the request was with a doctor, and that it would be actioned in due course. She also advised me to order on time in future and check my supplies.

I did not appreciate Emina’s tone during this interaction. Even though she noticed that I was visibly upset, she took no notice and continued repeating the same responses. While I understand that procedures must be followed, I found this approach unhelpful and dismissive.

It is very concerning that there appears to be no flexibility or escalation process for patients who urgently need their medication. Mistakes do happen, and patients can sometimes miscalculate supplies. However, patient well-being and safety should come first. In my view, there should be an option for urgent prescriptions in situations where a patient is completely out of medication and at risk of harm.

I am now immobile due to ongoing severly excruciating spinal pain that I have requested a referal to a spine specialist for, but no GP seems to be making this referral. Last week, I filled out the online form to request a telephone appointment, but no option to select an appointment was given. So I called up to explain and book the appointment over the phone. Instead of booking me an appointment while I was on the phone, I was told I would be sent a text message with a link to complete another online form to request this appointment. At the end of that form, I chose the option for a telephone appointment due to the fact that I am immobile. The following day, I received a call very early in the morning, which, unfortunately, I missed due to the fact that the strong pain relief medication I'm on makes me extremely sleepy. So I called up to explain that I had not had any prior communication to indicate that an appointment had been given to me for that time, therefore I hadn't been able to set an alarm to wake me up for the appointment. When the receptionist realised the severity of my pain, she kindly offered me a home appointment once she had run it by the practice manager. She then told me that it would be someone else who books the appointment and that they would call me back. The person who called to book my home visit appointment then tried to book me in for a face-to-face appointment, so I explained that I had been offered a home appointment and I explained the reasons why... I am homebound and immobile due to severe spinal pain, I can't move much at all, and I can't walk. I was eventually given the home visit appointment, with only the weekend to wait before being seen. The appointment was booked for this afternoon (Monday 2nd June 2025) at no specific time. My son (who has Autism and lives with me) changed his routine (which is not easy for him to do) in order to wait for the paramedic so that he could let them in as I am immobile. At 2:15 p.m., I received a call from the practice telling me that the paramedic is off work and consequently my appointment has to be cancelled... but then told me I could not book another home visit appointment. When I asked why, as it didn't make any sense, she just said the practice managers have decided I can't have a home visit. No reason was given for this. All I've been told is that they have suddenly made this decision. I was so shocked. It makes no sense at all that last week, I was offered this home visit, it was offered and approved by the practice (I didn't request it, I had requested a telephone appointment)... then the appointment was cancelled by the practice at the very last minute, and I can not rebook it because the practice has just 'decided' I can not have a home visit. I then said I would go ahead and book a telephone appointment as I could not get to the surgery for a face-to-face, and was told the earliest appointment I can have is at the end of June. This is for a patient who is unable to walk, is in severe pain, and whose strong pain relief medication is not helping the pain enough to enable mobility. I am expected to lay here for almost a month before I can even speak to a GP. By this point, I was exasperated, disappointed, and feeling cast aside and played with. I have struggled with the lack of compassion I've encountered at this practice, and today's experience has absolutely disgusted me. I can not stay here and most certainly would not recommend anyone joins. The practice building itself is run down, and the GPs are either clueless or uncaring, I have even had a GP sit there, giving no eye contact and not listening during a consultation. The physio is hopeless, and the appointment and prescription system is a complete shambles. This practice seriously needs investigating. Despite all the bad reviews, nothing is improving. To add insult to injury we eventually got a blood test and received a phone call from the clinic after we had already been confirmed with stage 4 cancer by Srepping Hill hospital. Just as the test for bowel cancer gave us the all clear only weeks before we received this devastating news. We”ve had a lot to deal with which is why this review is five months after the event but once we get through this terrible phase we will move away from this uncaring and unhelpful clinic. Ultimately the decision was made to safeguard against further health complications which could have developed from you having had broken any bones. Appointments are no longer booked at the reception desk. After 4pm the appointment request service closes until 8am on the next working day. The phones are left open 4pm until close for any urgent requests only. As your request was routine in nature you were advised to message using the online submission form the following day.

Unfortunately, you began to raise your voice, point, and talk over her. The receptionist manager came out to talk to you and reiterate the same information. We would like to politely remind you that we do not tolerate this behaviour.

We would like to apologise for any misinformation resulting in you being given a pot by another member of staff earlier on. We understand how this could have led you to believe you could still drop your sample for testing without raising a request to do so. 

 

We would like to assure you that patients who need help with the new system are encouraged to contact the practice via phone, so that they can be assisted through the process. We are always disappointed to hear that our patients have encountered frustrations with booking appointments. We have changed over to a new GP triage service where patients are guided through an online form which aims to obtain all relevant information from you. These questionnaires only take a few minutes to complete. 

 

Once complete these requests are reviewed by a GP onsite to assess and outcome. The outcomes are clinically guided and ensure we signpost to patients where they can receive the most appropriate care, this may not always need to be an appointment with the GP. This helps us see patients based upon clinical need as opposed to first come, first served. We implemented this new system after persistent feedback from our patients who expressed they no longer wanted the long phone waits. 

 

We appreciate you may feel as though you did not receive the correct care or advice from our service. If you did wish to discuss this further with us, please get in contact with the practice. The thing is though you can’t actually join another surgery that the crux of the matter, as it’s all about catchment zones even though people registered in the surgery don’t even live local in some cases.

I really don’t how they can sleep at night providing such a sub standard service all round to elderly and vulnerable people with health issues who in some cases need to make their way to the reception to be told “computer says now”

Bow your head in shame the seniors who run this practice it’s absolutely shocking!!!

*******Reply to cheadle medical practise reply on this review*****I have raised concerns previously with the practise on a number of occasions but they simply ignores patients concerns. The practise management simply rationalise problems raised, but don’t actually fix the issues to improve the services. I agree with another reviewer in that you have one front reception staff member who is simply rude with no customer communication skills. I speak with friends who live in neighbouring practices who do not have the same problems. It’s a complete joke that you cannot book an appointment online in the 21st century, then you can’t get through on the phone line or even if you are lucky to get through I’ve been told previously that 3-4 weeks for an appointment?? Cathy,

Thanks for your time in writing this. I can assure you that all complaints are taken seriously and handled by the appropriate answer. Our policy is that all complaints are responded to within 30 working days.

This is not the right forum to discuss written warnings but to be completely clear, we do not give patients warnings for raising complaints, the reason for any written warnings is laid out in the letter. If there are receptionists you feel have acted unprofessionally, if you can please let us know the specifics at gmicb-sto.mail.cheadlemedical@nhs.net we are happy to investigate further.

The accusation you make about medical mistakes is very serious, and I would be grateful for more detail sent to the e-mail above if you haven’t already as I’m sure you would want us to investigate this further.

Unfortunately, nationwide General Practice is under immense pressure and all of our team are doing their best to help under difficult circumstances. The number of appointments provided by practices has increased consistently, but the number of GPs in the country has decreased, and unfortunately there are only so many patients each GP can safely see in a day. We know this doesn’t keep up with the rising tide of demand, but we’re doing everything we can to see more patients safely. Generally in a week we offer up to a thousand appointments across our range of clinicians, but we have just under 12,000 patients and there is a lot of demand for those appointments, many are booked before the day, and some are emergency appointments in response to blood tests/hospital letters etc.

I’m sorry that you have not had a good experience at the practice, and hope this response addresses your When I had my baby, I was told by the hospital staff that a letter would be sent to my GP practice to register my daughter. A couple of weeks later I received a letter saying that an appointment had been made for her to have her first set of immunisations for a particular week, and I had to phone the practice to get the exact time and date.  The letter included my daughter's NHS number. So I went to the practice in person because it's impossible to get through by phone - bear in mind that I was recovering from a C section, so going there in person was not easy for me.  The receptionist almost had me in tears - she informed me that no, my daughter was not registered, and why on earth would I think such a thing? I explained that the hospital staff had told me that, to which she turned to her colleague and said with a laugh and a smirk on her face: 'Can you believe this lady thinks her baby is registered?!'   She also seemed surprised that I thought time had been reserved for a particular week for my daughter's immunisations (not a strange idea given that I had been sent a letter stating exactly that). She then proceeded to berate me because I asked for a repeat of my thyroxine prescription, to which she said that the hospital staff should have issued it, however they had correctly informed me that because I would be back on my pre-pregnancy dose that my GP was to issue it (again, she sneered 'why on earth would you think that?').
I am very much paraphrasing what happened here, but suffice to say, the receptionist's sneering attitude almost left me in tears, and I don't understand why someone who clearly hates dealing with patients works in a GP surgery. staff are always superb - I’m always seen to efficiently and by friendly doctors but the reception staff are honestly abysmal.
I understand we are very lucky to have the NHS and also understand staff are overworked and underpaid but I don’t believe there are any excuses for rude receptionists. If you don’t like talking to people or working on phones, work in a different sector. A few months back I rang up as I’d found out I was pregnant and did not want to continue with the pregnancy. The woman on the phone told me I could only see certain doctors, as doctors with certain religious backgrounds would not talk to me about termination. I ended up having to ring back for one reason or another and on the next call, same lady, I asked if I could book a doctors appointment with a doctor with no specific religion to discuss the issue - she laughed down the phone at me, obviously thinking im a racist. I felt myself go red with embarrassment and then hot with rage…I was only going off what she said so I spluttered ‘I don’t care what religion someone is…you just said certain doctors won’t speak to me because of the type of procedure…if they will see me I’ll happily attend’ - did I get an apology? No.
On both phone calls I was very distressed anyway, I was so anxious and so upset with my own personal problem and it was then made worse by the receptionist.
This is not the first bad experience I’ve had with them.

Sometimes when you call the doctors, you’re really going through it and the last thing you need is a cold harsh tone on the other end. It’s like a knife in an already sore wound.

You can really make a difference to someone that day  by just being kinder.",null,[0,211]]]],[null,null,null,null,null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/7806085126901456030/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiNDaFpEU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTmhYeTFEZUVSUkVBRRAA",[null,null,null,"/local/business/7806085126901456030/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiNDaFpEU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTmhYeTFEZUVSUkVBRRAA"],"https://business.google.com/local/business/7806085126901456030/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiNDaFpEU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTmhYeTFEZUVSUkVBRRAA",[null,null,null,"/local/business/7806085126901456030/customers/reviews/deletereply?p=CiNDaFpEU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTmhYeTFEZUVSUkVBRRAA"],null,"https://business.google.com/local/business/7806085126901456030/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiNDaFpEU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTmhYeTFEZUVSUkVBRRAA",[null,null,null,"/local/business/7806085126901456030/customers/reviews/reply?p=CiNDaFpEU1VoTk1HOW5TMFZKUTBGblNVTmhYeTFEZUVSUkVBRRAA"]],[null,null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/reviews/data=!4m8!14m7!1m6!2m5!1sChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNhXy1DeERREAE!2m1!1s0x0:0x2c5eda723a3dea2e!3m1!1s2@1:CIHM0ogKEICAgICa_-CxDQ%7C%7C?hl=en"],["https://www.google.com/local/content/rap/report?postId=ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNhXy1DeERREAE&t=1&entityid=ChZDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNhXy1DeERREi4KF0NJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdJQ2FfLUN4alFFEhNDZ3dJc01MVGlBWVFrUGE1cXdFGi0KFkNJSE0wb2dLRUlDQWdJQ2FfLUN4VFESE0Nnd0lzTUxUaUFZUWtQYTVxd0UiEgkAAAAAAAAAABEu6j06ctpeLCoTQ2d3SXNNTFRpQVlRa1BhNXF3RQ&wv=1&d=286732320",null,null,"0ahUKEwic2OnE2q6TAxUCHmMBHRrPNMcQoykIBygB"],null,[null,[[1,8]]]],"0ahUKEwic2OnE2q6TAxUCHmMBHRrPNMcQ0pMFCAUoAQ"],null,"CAESZENBRVEyQU1hUkVOcVJVbEJVa2x3UTJkdlFWQTNNa2xVUjJOR2MxbGZYMFZvUWxkcFQwUjNNRmx4YWs1SVkwcEpNR3RCUVVGQlFVZG5iamt6UVRoRGFFMWFkMWQ0WjFsQlEwbEI="],[["ChdDSUhNMG9nS0VJQ0FnSUNhcHRiNV93RRAB",["0x0:0x2c5eda723a3dea2e",null,1627635998984370,1627635998984370,[null,null,["https://www.google.com/maps/contrib/101512958041630330701/reviews?hl=en"],null,null,["Sofia If it’s not “urgent”, you can see a doctor you’ve never seen before,...I’ve not seen “my” doctor in years...and the record I had for a “none urgent” appointment was for in 4 weeks time. If it is urgent you then get asked by the receptionist what the problem is, which should not be the case. I don’t want to discuss my medical issues with a receptionist. The tone and attitude of the person I spoke to made it apparent that she obviously didn’t deem my problem to fit the criteria.\nI have seen 5 different Doctor’s over the last 9 months and have finally been referred to somebody who could identify the problem after being told something different every time by each doctor. Now thankfully that is managed and monitored, but you shouldn’t have to spend literally years feeling like you’re bothering them before somebody finally listens.\nI appreciate that the GP situation nationally is quite dire and I know they are over worked but if I was listened to the 1st time and referred instead of fobbed off, it would have saved literally hours of appointment time and a lot of
